scope: 2020-2025 historical and separately 2026 completed through Week9 point cutoff

featured.headline: A manager who keeps the market moving
featured.copy: The busiest trader in the documented 2020–2025 archive, Stew has 23 appearances on accepted deals. The 2025 Week 3 exchange with Stilly brought Jahmyr Gibbs and RJ Harvey, whose subsequent starts accounted for 302.10 points through Week 14. Volume and production are visible; net advantage over the players sent away remains unmeasured.

featured.headline: The blockbuster is rarely the final move
featured.copy: The 2024 Week 3 package from Thommy brought Terry McLaurin, De'Von Achane and Tank Dell, credited with 371.20 subsequent starting points through Week 14. Stilly's 2025 Chase acquisition and later three-team conversion illustrate the second act of a trade: receiving production, then deploying an asset in another negotiation.

featured.headline: An asset changes hands before kickoff
featured.copy: On August 30, 2021, Thommy acquired Josh Jacobs from Tony. The next day, Jacobs joined Lamar Jackson and Mark Andrews in a package sent to Birch, while Prescott, Fant and Gibson came back. This is a documented rapid flip, not proof that the entire second package can be valued as Jacobs' proceeds.

featured.headline: The opening-week swing of 2021
featured.copy: In a Week 1 exchange with Thommy, Tony brought in Corey Davis, A.J. Brown and Jonathan Taylor. Their subsequent credited starts supplied 378.70 points through Week 14, the largest observed single-deal return in Tony's reconstructed historical portfolio. The relative cost of sending Hill, Jacobs and Javonte Williams remains a separate question.

featured.headline: The price of moving two breakout receivers
featured.copy: The 2023 Week 3 deal with Stew placed James Conner, De'Von Achane and Puka Nacua on Kuhl's side, with 268.10 subsequent starting points recorded through Week 14. Lamb and Etienne later formed part of Stew's own trading chain, making this exchange an important starting point for a multi-manager trade-history analysis.

featured.headline: The historical archive still has stories to tell
featured.copy: Evans' 2021 Week 3 deal with Kuhl returned Aaron Rodgers and Keenan Allen, credited with 325.40 subsequent starter points through Week 14. His activity belongs in the historical member portfolio, not in the 2026 manager list; 2023 membership is attributed to Evans rather than JMid.

featured.headline: Fournette's second stop
featured.copy: Stover acquired Leonard Fournette from Kuhl in 2021 Week 5. Fournette contributed 154.60 subsequent starting points through Week 14, Stover's largest recorded single-trade player return in the represented archive. Stover also appears as Gurt in the current league; the aliases refer to the same manager.

featured.headline: A three-player package that defined a season's scoring record
featured.copy: Birch's August 31, 2021 deal with Thommy brought Lamar Jackson, Mark Andrews and Josh Jacobs. Their starts totaled 501.68 points through Week 14, with another 103.80 in Weeks 15–17. The team lost its Week 15 matchup, so that production is not evidence of a championship run caused by the trade.

featured.headline: Barkley headlines a 2022 exchange
featured.copy: Mitch received Saquon Barkley and Adam Thielen from Stilly in 2022 Week 2. Their subsequent starts produced 239.00 points through Week 14, his largest measured single-deal return in this window. A received-player points record is not a verdict on the deal's price or longer-term outcome.

featured.headline: From acquisition to conversion
featured.copy: JMid's leading historical return was the 2024 Week 2 deal that acquired Kyren Williams and Calvin Ridley, producing 180.70 subsequent starter points through Week 14. In the later Chase chain, JMid kept Chase using a 2026 first-round pick before transferring him in October 2026; keeper opportunity cost belongs alongside any downstream return.

featured.headline: A short but documented trade ledger
featured.copy: The current 2020–2025 transaction archive records one Koble trade appearance: the 2021 Week 4 acquisition of Zack Moss and James Robinson from Tony. Those players produced 120.30 subsequent starter points through Week 14. A one-trade sample is not enough to characterize a manager's trading skill.

featured.headline: A new chapter begins in 2026
featured.copy: Scott made no recorded completed trade in the 2020–2025 Sleeper archive. On September 1, 2026, he sent Ladd McConkey to Stew and received Emeka Egbuka. Egbuka has 48.30 starting points in strictly later completed weeks through Week 9; that is an observed return, not a complete trade benefit assessment.

rules: Do not claim win/loss caused by deal without counterfactual data.
Descriptive posttrade starts do not represent net benefits.
